text: Suppose your magical time-stopping pocket watch somehow protects your lungs and warms your body with an invisible field.
Even then, celestial mechanics has prepared an unavoidable death sentence.
Right now, at this very moment, you feel like you are sitting completely still.
The surface of the Earth is rotating on its axis at roughly sixteen hundred kilometers per hour.
More dramatically, planet Earth is hurtling around the Sun at an astronomical orbital speed of thirty kilometers per second—over one hundred and eight thousand kilometers per hour.
When you pause time for the universe, the Earth's orbital trajectory halts instantaneously.
But because you are the solitary observer exempt from the time freeze, the sacred law of physical inertia guarantees that your mass must preserve its momentum.
The precise microsecond time freezes, you would be violently catapulted forward relative to the planet's surface at thirty kilometers per second.
To put that in perspective, that is Mach eighty-eight.
At thirty kilometers per second, you would instantly slam into the frozen atmospheric wall.

The resulting kinetic impact would unleash more explosive energy than a tactical nuclear warhead, utterly disintegrating your cellular structure into an incandescent cloud of ionized plasma before your nervous system could even send a single pain signal to your brain.
